title: Earnings management and the market performance of acquiring firms

rival_explanations: overoptimistic expectation hypothesis (the elevated abnormal accruals of stock-for-stock acquirers reflect optimistic growth expectations rather than deliberate earnings management)
the abnormal-accrual/abnormal-return correlation reflects contemporaneous earnings-announcement effects rather than pre-merger earnings management
overoptimistic expectation hypothesis (the negative accrual/long-term-return relation reflects the unraveling of overly optimistic growth expectations rather than the reversal of earnings management)
the general accrual anomaly of Sloan (1996) (accruals predict long-term returns for all firms, so the effect is not specific to stock-for-stock mergers)

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (publicly traded U.S. nonfinancial firms across manufacturing, communications, business services, and other SIC industries; financial firms excluded)
context.sample_description: Completed mergers of publicly traded U.S. companies, restricted to pure stock swaps or pure cash purchases with nonfinancial acquirers, obtained from the Security Data Company (SDC) online database of domestic mergers and acquisitions, with required quarterly data on Compustat, returns on CRSP, and CEO-ownership/board data from WRDS executive compensation database and SEC filings (LexisNexis Academic)
